Log in to check out faster. Continue shopping ABOUT US We are a fashion multi designer store that believes in bringing timeless, elegant pieces that empower individuals to express their unique style. Our commitment to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction drives everything we do. OUR STORY Two journeys, one table, and a cup of tea that changed everything. After walking our own paths and experiencing different chapters of life, we finally sat down one evening and asked ourselves—what if we build something together? What started as simple conversations over endless cups of tea slowly turned into ideas, and those ideas grew into a shared belief. We didn’t know how far we would go, but we knew we wanted to create something bigger than where we came from. That belief became Trovelle—an online marketplace for designer wear clothing, built with the vision of bringing beautiful, thoughtfully designed fashion from talented designers to people who truly appreciate it. And this is just the beginning of our journey. as2hrk2xrc2zlwvvzstwocolumnblock1 RUPAL GUPTA I’ve always been someone who chooses the best in life and constantly pushes myself to grow. For the past 10 years, I built my career as an Engineering Manager, leading teams, solving complex problems, and thriving in the corporate world. I was a full-on corporate slay… until the day my company suddenly shut down. In that moment, everything paused, and I found myself standing at a crossroad—play it safe or take a leap of faith. I chose the scarier path: to believe in myself and build something bigger than just a job title, something louder than my fears. That’s the reason I created this marketplace—to turn uncertainty into opportunity and build something meaningful of my own. CHAVI KANSAL I’ve always been a young, optimistic girl who believes life is full of opportunities waiting to be explored. In my early years, I was a corporate girlie—driven by targets, meetings, and big ambitions. Then life evolved, and I stepped into new roles as a homemaker and the proud mother of a beautiful daughter. While these roles shaped me in many ways, one dream always stayed constant—the desire to create something meaningful, something I could nurture and grow every single day. Not just a business, but a beginning I chose for myself. And that’s exactly why I started this marketplace—this is the start of my entrepreneurial journey. This guide covers everything you need to put together the perfect Diwali ethnic wear looks for 2026. What to Wear for Diwali: The Basics Colour matters. Traditional Diwali colours include deep reds, royal blues, emerald greens, mustard yellows, and gold. Fabric sets the occasion. Puja calls for something graceful and traditional; the evening party invites more drama and shine. Comfort is non-negotiable. You will be sitting, standing, lighting diyas, eating, so your outfit needs to move with you. Diwali Outfit Ideas for 2026 1. The Embroidered Suit Set A classic for a reason. An embroidered suit set in jewel tones, deep wine, midnight blue, or emerald green, hits the sweet spot between traditional and refined. Pair with statement jhumkas and a potli bag. Shop our Festive Wear collection . 2. The Farshi Salwar Set The farshi salwar's floor-sweeping hem creates instant drama without requiring heavy embellishment. Opt for an ombre farshi in dusty rose or burnt orange for a modern Diwali look that photographs beautifully. 3. The Co-Ord Set in Festive Colours For Diwali parties and friends' gatherings, a festive co-ord set in rich brocade or printed fabric is effortlessly chic. Browse Co-Ord Sets . 4. The Cape Set A cape jacket set layered over a matching kurta and pant is the Diwali party outfit of the moment. The cape adds drama, the co-ordinated base keeps it grounded. 5. The Kaani Suit Set For those who want something deeply rooted in Indian craft traditions, a Kaani jacquard suit set is unmatched. Shop Kaani Suit Sets . While traditional wear is always a beautiful choice, there’s a fresh trend on the rise— Indo-Western outfits . These striking ensembles perfectly blend Eastern elegance and Western chic, giving you the best of both worlds. Gone are the days when Diwali meant sticking to only traditional lehengas or sarees. Today’s fashion scene allows you to experiment, combine, and redefine festive wear. So, why not step out of your comfort zone this Diwali and explore the world of Indo-Western outfits for women ? Whether attending a family puja, hosting a Diwali dinner, or partying with friends, there’s an Indo-Western look for every occasion. Here are 10 stunning Indo-Western outfit ideas that will ensure you sparkle and stand out this Diwali. Let’s dive right into it! 1. The Fiery Red Co-Ord Set – Effortless Elegance with a Dash of Festivity First on the list is a vibrant red co-ord set that perfectly blends elegance with modern style. Co-ord sets have become immensely popular for their easy-to-wear yet fashionable appeal. This ensemble features a matching top and wide-legged trousers, offering comfort and sophistication. The beauty of this Indo-Western outfit lies in its simplicity. The tailored cut of the trousers balances the flowy top, creating a streamlined, effortlessly chic look. Perfect for Diwali parties or family gatherings, the bright red hue immediately adds a festive flair, while the minimalistic design ensures you remain comfortable throughout the night. Styling Tip : Pair this ethnic co-ord set with statement earrings and sleek heels for a modern, polished look. Want to amp up the Diwali vibe? Add a bold red lipstick to complete your stunning ensemble. 2. The Glamorous Wine Corset Set – A Fusion of Structure and Flow Looking for something that has the wow factor? Enter the Wine corset set , a luxurious Indo-Western outfit for Diwali that combines the best of both worlds—Western corsetry and traditional Indian silhouettes. The fitted corset-style bodice beautifully complements the flowing skirt, creating a glamorous yet refined look perfect for evening events. Corset-inspired outfits have been dominating the designer Indo-Western outfit scene, and for a good reason—they highlight your figure while adding an element of drama to your ensemble. This deep burgundy piece is ideal for women who want to step out in something unique yet festive. Styling Tip : With this outfit, keep accessories minimal since the corset adds plenty of detail. Opt for soft waves or a sleek bun, and let the rich colour and structure of the outfit speak for itself. 3. The Classic Sharara Set – Timeless Festive Glam No Diwali wardrobe is complete without a fabulous sharara set , and this red embroidered sharara set is as festive as possible. Sharara sets have been integral to Indian festive wear for centuries, but today’s designers have given them a contemporary twist. The wide-legged pants and an intricately embroidered kurta make this sharara set for women a must-have for the festive season. The standout feature of this outfit is its detailed embroidery, which adds a touch of grandeur without going overboard. The sharara’s flared pants allow for easy movement, whether you’re dancing at a Diwali party or performing a traditional puja. Styling Tip : To complete the festive look, pair this outfit with bold gold jewellery and strappy sandals. For makeup, go for a soft glow with a hint of shimmer on the eyes, letting your outfit take centre stage. 4. The Royal Red Dhoti Kurta Set – Bold, Beautiful, and Unconventional Want to mix things up? The dhoti kurta set for women is a bold choice that will turn heads this Diwali. This look combines the relaxed comfort of the dhoti with the structured elegance of a fitted kurta. The result? A dhoti set that’s modern, comfortable, and fashion-forward. The rich purple hue of this dhoti kurta set adds a regal touch, while the fluid drape of the dhoti keeps things playful and easygoing. Whether hosting a Diwali dinner or attending a close-knit family gathering, this outfit will ensure you’re the centre of attention for all the right reasons. A patterned cape. Suddenly, getting dressed feels a lot more interesting. Winter layers don't have to hide your personal style; they can be the detail that brings an outfit together. The secret isn't piling on more. It's choosing one strong layer, giving it a simple foundation and making sure the whole look works when you move. From flowing capes to defined jackets and patterned coats, here's how to make your winter wardrobe work a little harder, without making dressing feel like work. Start simple. Let the layer do the talking. When a cape or jacket has plenty of pattern, the easiest supporting outfit is often the quietest. Try a plain top and trousers in one colour, then add a layer with paisley, embroidery or a contrasting border. This isn't a rule against mixing prints. It's a useful starting point when you're short on time or want a favourite piece to stand out. Browse capes, jackets and coats for women and imagine each one over clothes already in your wardrobe. The cape: relaxed shape, plenty of presence Aafreen Paisley Open Cape: a patterned layer over a quiet, tonal base. A flowing cape can make simple separates feel considered without requiring a complicated outfit underneath. Let the shoulders and arm shape provide the movement, and keep the neckline free of accessories that compete with the pattern. The Aafreen Paisley Open Cape is listed in a wool blend. Its current product image pairs a black-ground paisley design with black wide-leg trousers, an easy example of a detailed layer over a tonal base. Try the same idea with a plain top, trousers you enjoy wearing and a compact bag. If you prefer a narrower outline, swap the wide trousers for a straighter pair. The aim is balance that feels like you, not following one formula for every body. Make it yours Pick up one colour from the cape in your earrings or bag, or keep every supporting piece neutral. Before heading out, check that you can carry your bag and reach forward comfortably. A striking silhouette still needs to work beyond the mirror. The jacket: an instant change of mood Embroidery at the shoulders and cuffs adds detail to a defined black silhouette. A defined jacket gives a simple base more structure. Wear it over a quiet top and trousers for a polished daytime outfit, or try it with a dress when you want a different shape from your usual cardigan. The Merino Wool Black Jacket is listed with a wool-blend fabric specification. Its current photograph shows a zip front, stand collar and tonal embroidery at the upper body and cuffs. Pair it with plain trousers to keep those details in focus. Pay attention to the shoulder fit and sleeve room. The jacket should accommodate the top or knit you actually intend to wear underneath, not only a thin fitting-room layer. A sharp outline loses its appeal if you can't sit or raise your arms comfortably. One colour is enough to connect the look You don't need an exact match between your jacket and the rest of the outfit. Repeat one colour from its pattern, or use a neutral base that lets the detailing stand apart. If the jacket's front is busy, try smaller jewellery and a quieter bag. Then comes the question: is hand embroidery worth choosing over machine embroidery? The useful answer isn't a blanket yes or no. It depends on what you value, how the garment is made and how you plan to wear it. When comparing hand embroidery vs machine embroidery, start with the process rather than assuming one label guarantees better quality. The design, materials, finishing and condition of the garment matter too. This guide focuses on buying decisions; for an introduction to regional traditions, explore our story of hand-embroidered ethnic wear . Hand embroidery vs machine embroidery: the short answer Hand embroidery is worked with stitches placed by a person using a needle or a hand-operated embroidery tool. Machine embroidery uses a machine to form the stitches; the design may be guided by an operator or controlled through a programmed pattern. Both can produce beautiful results, and both require skill at different stages. Choose hand embroidery when the particular handworked technique and the making process matter to you. Choose machine embroidery when you like its finish and it suits your needs. In either case, judge the whole garment rather than the label alone. What the product description should tell you A useful description identifies the fabric, the embroidery method where known, the areas decorated and the pieces included. A hand-embroidered neckline doesn't necessarily mean the sleeves, trouser borders and dupatta were made in the same way. Likewise, hand embellished isn't interchangeable with hand embroidered. It may refer to decorations attached by hand over another form of surface work. If the distinction matters to you, ask which parts were stitched, embellished or finished by hand. Can an outfit combine hand and machine work? Yes. A garment can bring together machine-stitched motifs, hand-attached embellishments and hand finishing. A mixed process isn't automatically a compromise in quality. What matters is that the description makes the work clear and that you're happy with the result. The same principle applies across a coordinated set. The kurta, trousers and dupatta may use different techniques to achieve different effects. Ask about each component rather than extending a claim from one detail to the entire outfit. How the finished embroidery can differ Repetition and variation Machine embroidery can produce closely repeated motifs with consistent stitch placement. Hand embroidery may show small variations between motifs. Those differences can be part of its character, but they aren't a reliable authentication test on their own. Skilled handwork can be exceptionally regular, and machine work can create complex textures. A slightly uneven flower doesn't prove that an outfit was hand embroidered, just as a neat border doesn't prove it was made by machine. Texture and surface detail The raised or flat appearance of embroidery depends on the stitches, threads, layering and supporting materials. Both hand and machine methods can create textured surfaces. Instead of judging the technique from depth alone, look at how the detailing suits the fabric and the way the garment hangs. Placement and balance Check where motifs sit around seams, necklines and cuffs. Do the borders look intentional? Does a heavily decorated area pull the fabric out of shape? Placement and finishing affect the overall result, whatever method formed the stitches. Also consider how the design will look when worn, not only laid flat. An ornate neckline might be hidden beneath your preferred shawl, while embellished cuffs could be the detail you notice most throughout the evening. Why prices can be different Hand embroidery can involve substantial skilled labour, particularly for detailed or densely worked designs. Machine embroidery can make repeated patterns more efficient to produce. However, that doesn't mean every hand-embroidered garment costs more than every machine-embroidered one. Fabric, thread, embellishments, construction, design complexity and the amount of embroidery all contribute to price. Compare the whole outfit and the specificity of the product description, not just a single craft label. Avoid treating a fixed number of production hours as typical for every embroidered suit. This guide focuses specifically on wedding guests, from haldi to reception. For broader festival and party dressing, see our kurta-pajama guide for special occasions . What should male guests wear to an Indian wedding? Start with a coordinated kurta set, then adjust the level of detail to the invitation. A lighter, simpler outfit can suit a daytime celebration; an embroidered kurta or jacket combination can feel more dressed up for the evening. These are styling suggestions, not rules for every Indian wedding. Explore men's wedding kurta sets to compare coordinated looks. Before choosing, check whether the hosts have requested particular colours, a theme or specific formalwear. Religious ceremonies may have requirements around modesty, footwear or head coverings, so ask your hosts when unsure. Choose your outfit by wedding function Haldi: keep things light and uncomplicated Choose a comfortable kurta with trousers that let you sit and move easily. Yellow is an option if it fits the invitation, but it isn't compulsory for every haldi. If turmeric or water will be part of the celebration, wear something you won't worry about getting marked. Save delicate embroidery and treasured accessories for another function. Mehendi: colour without too much weight A printed or lightly embroidered kurta is a relaxed choice for a mehendi. Soft shades work well in daylight, while richer tones can suit an evening gathering. Consider how long you'll be wearing it: a comfortable neckline and room through the shoulders matter more than an elaborate finish. Sangeet: dress for movement A Nehru-style jacket over a simple kurta gives the look definition. Alternatively, let an embroidered kurta be the main detail and keep the rest quiet. Try the complete outfit before the event: raise your arms, sit down and take a few dance steps. An outfit that only works while standing still is not your best sangeet companion. Wedding ceremony: let the setting guide you For a daytime ceremony, consider a lighter or mid-tone kurta set with restrained detailing. For an evening ceremony, deeper shades and more visible embroidery are options. Your role matters too: close family may coordinate with the couple, while guests can keep their look celebratory without matching the groom's level of formality. Reception: add polish, not clutter If Indian ethnic wear suits the reception dress code, a coordinated jacket, kurta and trouser combination is an easy choice. Let one feature lead, whether that's the jacket's pattern or the kurta's embroidery. If the invitation specifies Western formalwear or black tie, follow that request instead. A navy kurta set for an understated guest look Contrasting embroidery adds detail to a simple navy base without overwhelming the outfit. The Classic Navy Embroidered Kurta & Pant for Men offers a visual reference for this quieter approach: coordinated navy separates with contrast detail at the collar, placket and cuffs. Check the product's fabric, fit and care information before deciding whether it suits your venue and weather. Choose fabric and layers for the actual weather For a warm outdoor venue, prioritise a breathable fabric, comfortable lining and a fit that doesn't cling. For cooler evenings, consider a more substantial layer that you can remove indoors. Don't judge warmth by sheen or richness alone; check the individual garment's fabric composition. If the itinerary moves between an outdoor ceremony and an indoor dinner, plan your layers around both. Carrying a removable jacket or shawl is often more practical than wearing an outfit that feels too warm throughout the day. How to wear a shawl with a wedding kurta Wedding shawls for men can add colour, texture and an extra layer. Drape one over a shoulder for a relaxed finish, or wrap it around both shoulders when seated outdoors. Keep the ends off the floor and clear of anything they might catch on. With a patterned jacket, choose a quieter shawl. With a plain kurta, let the shawl provide the main detail. There's no need to combine bold embroidery, a statement jacket and an ornate shawl in one outfit. Check fit and footwear before the celebration

This season, we're turning to the makers we know best: artisans across India who still work in techniques passed down over generations. Kashmiri paper mache painters. IKKIVI COLLECTION THE GIFT SHOP Your Resort-Ready Capsule Resort trips and warm-weather getaways all ask the same quiet question: what do you actually pack so you're not living out of a suitcase, rewearing the same three things, or carrying clothes that wrinkle the second they come out of your bag? A capsule approach solves it. Instead of packing outfit by outfit, you pack a small set of pieces: breathable fabrics, easy silhouettes, a tight color story. These pieces mix and match into a full week (or two) of looks, whether you're island hopping in the Bahamas, poolside at a resort, or working your way through a warm climate city break. This guide walks you through how to build that capsule, what fabrics actually hold up to travel and heat, and which pieces from IKKIVI's resort and travel edits are built for exactly this kind of trip. They're ethically made, in sizes 2XS to 5XL. Why Linen (and Natural Fibers) Are the Resort-Wear MVP If there's one fabric decision that makes or breaks your warm-weather packing list, it's choosing natural, breathable fibers over synthetics. Linen in particular has become the go-to for resort and travel wardrobes, for a few concrete reasons: It breathes. Linen is a looser weave natural fiber, so air moves through it. It won't trap heat against your skin the way polyester or other synthetics do, which matters directly in humid, tropical climates. It handles heat and humidity well. Linen absorbs moisture and releases it quickly, so it feels drier against your skin in hot, sticky weather than most synthetic blends. The lived-in wrinkle is part of the look. Linen creases naturally. That relaxed, slightly rumpled look is part of its appeal for travel and resort settings, so you don't need to fight it. You can style it down or up easily. The same linen piece works for a beach walk at noon and a dinner reservation at eight, with a swap of shoes and jewelry. You'll find exactly this in IKKIVI's Linen edit : 100% linen tops, trousers, dresses, and sets designed for warm climates, alongside organic cotton and other natural-fiber pieces across the Resort Wear and Travel Easy collections. Build Your Capsule: 5 Pieces That Do the Work You don't need twelve outfits. You need five to seven pieces that combine into twelve. Here's how to think about the categories, with real options you can shop right now. 1. The Linen Co-ord Set (your beach-to-dinner uniform) A matching linen or linen-blend top-and-bottom set is the single most efficient resort packing choice: it reads as a finished outfit on its own, and each piece also works separately with something else in your bag. Zulu Black Linen Pant Set and Zulu Blue Linen Pant Set : shirt-and-trouser linen sets built for exactly this kind of mix-and-match travel styling. Sahara Linen Crop Top & Skirt Set : a lighter, cropped silhouette for daytime heat. You can browse the full range in Co-ord Sets . 2. The One-and-Done Jumpsuit A jumpsuit is the closest thing to packing an outfit instead of a garment. Zero matching is required, and it looks considered the moment you put it on. Pack one in a print and one in a solid, and you've covered most of a week's dinners. Evening Chai Jumpsuit : an easy, relaxed silhouette. Ikat Jumpsuit and Ocean Patch Jumpsuit : pattern-driven pieces that work as your trip's statement outfit. Oceanarium Jumpsuit and Sweet Lavender Jumpsuit : softer colorways for daytime wear. Blue Daisy Day Jumpsuit and Ivory Daisy Day Jumpsuit : lighter prints suited to daytime resort settings. You'll find the complete range in Jumpsuits & Rompers . 3. Breathable Linen Separates (the mix-and-match workhorses) Separates are what actually stretch your capsule. One top can pair with two or three bottoms across a trip. Indigo Splash Linen Shirt paired with its matching Indigo Splash Linen Pants : wear them together or split them across different outfits. The Ghar Linen Trousers and The Neev Linen Trousers : versatile linen trousers you can rotate under multiple tops. The Ghar Linen Peplum Top : a structured top you can dress down with shorts by day and dress up with trousers at night. Ocean Breeze Linen Pants : a lightweight bottom built for warm-climate wear. 4. One Statement Dress for Dinner Every resort capsule earns one dress that's a little more special. Pack light everywhere else so you have room for this one. Golden Palm Linen Dress : a linen maxi dress designed as an easy dinner-ready piece. 5. Color and Print for Vacation Energy Resort wardrobes lean into color in a way your everyday wardrobe doesn't. That color is part of what signals vacation rather than work trip. IKKIVI's Leheriya tie-dye sets are built specifically around this: Candy Leheriya Co-ord Set , Ocean Leheriya Co-ord Set , and Tropical Leheriya Co-ord Set : tie-dye print sets in distinct colorways. Leheriya Blue Co-ord and Sunrise Tie & Dye Co-ord Set : more tie-dye options for a vacation-forward palette. Strappy Hills (Set of 2) and Void Panzo Set : additional set options for rounding out your color story. You'll find more curated travel picks across dresses, jumpsuits, and jackets in the Travel Easy edit . Founded in London in 2012, Aashni + Co began with a boutique in Notting Hill, becoming one of the earliest destinations outside India, in our experience, to champion authenticated creations from the country's most celebrated designers, including Sabyasachi . Today, the luxury platform curates a portfolio of, by our own count, over 100 leading Indian fashion houses, serving a global clientele across the UK, India, the UAE, the US, Canada, Australia, Singapore and Europe. Defined by a commitment to authenticity and craftsmanship, every designer featured on Aashni + Co is personally vetted, with each purchase accompanied by a designer-issued invoice. Complementing its curated offering is a bespoke styling service, available through private consultations in London and Mumbai, as well as virtual appointments for clients worldwide, delivering a seamless and highly personalised luxury shopping experience. Luxury Indian fashion is not a single thing Luxury Indian fashion is not a single thing. It is a world of extraordinary range from Sabyasachi's heritage bridal lehengas, hand-embroidered over thousands of hours, to Torani 's joyful printed separates designed for effortless everyday dressing, to Gaurav Gupta 's sculptural gowns seen on red carpets from Mumbai to Los Angeles. What connects these designers is not a single occasion, aesthetic or customer. What connects them is craftsmanship, intention and the understanding that clothing carries meaning.
